newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Tests set for possible leprosy vaccine.
newsitem.headline: Tests set for possible leprosy vaccine.

text.p: Venezuelan doctors said on Wednesday they will begin human tests this year on a potential vaccine for leprosy, the wasting disease that affects over one million people worldwide.
"The vaccine does not have a patent, nor will it," said Jacinto Covit, who heads the research team at Venezuela's National Hygiene Institute which developed the drug, the first of its kind.

"We developed it for under-developed countries to use," he told reporters. Covit, whose research programme is supported by the World Health Organisation (WHO), said the vaccine had been derived from an infected armadillo, and then mixed with the anti-tuberculosis drug BCG.

Leprosy is a progressive disease that attacks the skin and nerves, causing blotches and lumps, and can cause numbness, paralysis and ultimately deformity. It is related to the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.
Trials on some 2,000 Venezuelans that recently come in contact with the bacterium that causes the ailment will begin over the next six months, Covit said, with a further 40,000 tests next year.
According to WHO figures, there are 1.2 million known cases of leprosy in the world, nearly half of them in India.
